page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v7 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per thread. Hardware-level features include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, 480 MB of shared L3 cache, and support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX-Tile, AMX-INT8, and cryptographic accelerators including AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded data processing, recording 32.64 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.59 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Single-core compute capability reflects average tier performance with a stress-ng score of 2192.59. However, aggregate multi-threaded compute and uncached memory throughput are constrained by the two-vCPU hardware footprint, with stress-ng multi-core testing at 2274.79 and large-block memory write speeds measuring 12.39 GB/sec. The instance includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and no GPU accelerators, requiring external network-attached Premium Storage for persistent filesystems.

Due to its resource density and strong per-core instruction throughput, the D2s_v7 delivers balanced qualitative efficiency for modest deployments. It is suited for foundational infrastructure tasks such as lightweight web serving, application microservices, development environments, and small-scale caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure D2s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core, 8.0 GB of RAM, 480 MB of L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent workloads. In benchmark tests, the D2s_v7 demonstrates strong single-threaded compression performance, achieving 32.64 GB/sec in gzip, while multi-core computational throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained by the dual-thread allocation. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, this instance is suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, modest Redis caching tiers, CI/CD runners, and staging deployments.
